current_status.from: Active through December 2026 [VERIFY: no rescission action captured 2026-04-29]
current_status.to: Active through approximately December 2026; no rescission found. A Data Center Advisory Committee (one trustee, one zoning board member, one BZA member, the zoning inspector, and 10 residents), formed January 2026, presented its findings to the Zoning Board on 2026-05-12, recommending a new M-3 Industrial zoning classification with tiered regulations, bonding/escrow requirements, and a formal process; the zoning board voted 6-0 to move the proposal to the Lucas County Plan Commission for review.
current_status.reason: Township zoning board's own May 12, 2026 special meeting minutes record the committee's presentation, its recommendations, and the unanimous vote to advance the M-3 zoning proposal -- confirming the moratorium remains in force while the follow-up zoning process (anticipated by the original 12-month term) proceeds.

evidence.title: For 18 months, Alliance won't permit new data center construction
evidence.supports: Confirms the 18-month moratorium, 5-1 vote, date of the council meeting, and context (mid-June I-2 zoning restriction, sub-committee formation).
evidence.quote: ALLIANCE - No new data centers will be built in Alliance for 18 months after City Council approved a moratorium at its July 6 meeting. The temporary ban - not to exceed 18 months - was approved by a 5-1 vote. ... Councilman Phillip Mastroianni voted against the legislation. Councilwoman Jennifer Kiko was absent. ... The ban also follows separate legislation council approved in mid-June to restrict future data centers to I-2 industrial zones.
